28.0.0.en: The hearts of Christ's followers were attached to Him, but the Sabbath kept them from going out to Him, because it is the day of rest for the Jews. At the dawn of Sunday, two of the women hurried to the tomb, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary, who is thought to be the wife of Clopas, the sister of the Virgin Mary, and perhaps she is the Virgin herself. But Matthew did not mention this, because he wrote his Gospel for the Jews, who do not accept the testimony of relatives. The two wished to cast even a glance at the tomb of their beloved, with whom the Magdalene had lived for more than three years.

28.1.0.en: Because of the two women's love for Christ in visiting His tomb, He granted them more than they could imagine. When they arrived at the tomb, a great angel appeared with a strong light; Church tradition says that he was the archangel Michael, who had come to announce the resurrection to humanity. He rolled the great stone away from the tomb, and there was an earthquake, a symbol of the shaking and fall of earthly lusts and the beginning of the new life for the children of God who believe in His resurrection, and the angel sat on the stone in great splendor.

28.1.1.en: Christ had risen before that and no human being had seen Him, and the stone was still placed on the tomb at His resurrection. Then the angel Michael came to announce the good news of the resurrection, and he rolled away the stone so that the empty tomb would be seen.

28.1.2.en: Be confident that for every love you offer to God, He gives you in return blessings and love that you cannot imagine. So do not despise your small prayers, or your readings even if your understanding of them is limited, or your services however secondary they may seem, for God cares for them, indeed they are very precious to Him, and He rewards you for them with blessings you do not expect.

28.2.0.en: The appearance of the angel was great, with an inexpressible light; here St. Matthew likens it to lightning in its brightness, and his garments to snow in their whiteness. The guards of the tomb were afraid of his appearance, and of the earthquake, and also of the rolling away of the stone; for the power of God is fearful to the wicked.

28.3.0.en: The fear was for the wicked guards, but the two Marys, who loved Christ, the angel reassures and gives them the good news of His resurrection, and describes Him as the crucified One. He is the crucified and the risen One, for this title shows His love that gave itself even to death, and at the same time His power by His rising from the dead. And he offers them the proof of His resurrection, which is the empty tomb.

28.4.0.en: The two angels granted the two Marys to announce the resurrection to the disciples of Christ and that He would appear to them in Galilee, which is in the north of Judea, where He was accustomed to walk with them, teach and work miracles. The two women went out with great fear because of the greatness of the sight and of the announcement. At the same time, they went out with wondrous joy, for they received what they had not expected or imagined, which was the return of their beloved to them by His resurrection. This means that the previous conversation took place inside the tomb, that is, the angel, after rolling away the stone and sitting on it, entered the tomb and gave the good news to the two Marys. The two Marys hurried to the disciples to announce it to them.

28.4.1.en: Thus the woman was changed from one who drove the man to sin in the Garden of Eden into a herald of the resurrection and the new life in Christ.

28.4.2.en: Love changes you from evil to good if you turn it into acts of worship and service, and God rejoices in you. This was the first of the visits to the tomb, and the visits can be arranged as follows, as St. Peter El-Sadamanti indicated:

28.4.3.en: (1) The visit of the two Marys, one of whom was the Magdalene, as Matthew mentioned (vv. 1-8). Matthew did not mention the other woman because she was either the Lady the Virgin or Mary the wife of Clopas, the mother of James and Joses, who is the aunt of Christ, and the testimony of the two is not counted because they are relatives of Christ. In this visit they saw Christ and held His feet.

28.4.4.en: (2) The second visit is the one mentioned in (Jn 20:1), in which we find the Magdalene visiting the tomb alone, and she found the stone taken away from the tomb. Note what John mentioned, that it was still dark, which means not complete darkness over the whole earth, but the presence of darkness in the western side of the earth, while on the eastern side the light of day had appeared, that is, dawn had broken.

28.4.5.en: (3) The third visit was by the Magdalene, for when she returned to Jerusalem, she told the disciples as the angel had told her, so Peter and John went out with her and saw the tomb empty, then departed believing in His resurrection. But she remained alone before the tomb, and saw Christ, and He said to her:

28.4.7.en: (4) The fourth visit was made by the Magdalene with a group of women, among whom were mentioned Mary the mother of James and Joses and also Joanna, and other people were with them. It took place at early dawn, and they saw the tomb empty and heard the good news of the two angels (Lk 24:1-10).

28.4.8.en: (5) The fifth and last visit was at sunrise, and in it the Magdalene went, and with her Mary the mother of James and Joses and Salome the mother of the sons of Zebedee, and they saw the tomb empty and heard the good news of the angel (Mk 16:1-8).

28.5.0.en: God's blessings to those who love Him increase, so the risen Christ Himself appears to the two and gives them peace, a gift unique to the children of God above all the world. In the excess of their joy, they held His feet and worshiped Him in humility. For Christ's love for us draws us to worship Him in humility, and to experience Him and touch Him in our lives. Then He confirmed their being sent to announce the good news to the Church in the person of the disciples, because of His love for them, for they were the first to visit the tomb.

28.5.1.en: How wonderful!... The mighty Christ, risen from the dead, humbles Himself and calls His disciples His brethren, and even goes before them to Galilee and waits for them to rejoice in meeting them and to make them rejoice in Him.

28.5.2.en: “Be not afraid”: to reassure the two women, for feelings of fear and joy were mingled within them, as they had not expected to see Christ risen, and this was the first appearance of Christ after His resurrection.

28.5.3.en: The appearances that the Holy Bible mentions of Christ after His resurrection and until His ascension are as follows: (1) His appearance to Mary Magdalene and the other Mary, who is probably the Lady the Virgin (Mt 28:9; Mk 16:9).

28.5.4.en: (2) His appearance to Mary Magdalene alone, when He said to her: “Touch Me not” (Jn 20:14-17).

28.5.6.en: (4) His appearance to the two disciples of Emmaus on the day of the resurrection (Mk 16:12; Lk 24:15). (5) His appearance to the disciples on the evening of the day of the resurrection in the upper room (Lk 24:36), and John the Evangelist mentioned that Thomas was not with them (Jn 20:19-24). (6) His appearance to them also in the upper room eight days after the previous appearance, when Thomas was with them (Jn 20:26).

28.5.7.en: (7) His appearance to the disciples in Galilee at the Sea of Tiberias (Jn 21:1).

28.5.8.en: (8) His appearance to the disciples in Galilee (v. 16).

28.5.9.en: (9) His appearance to more than 500 brethren at once (1 Cor 15:6).

28.5.10.en: (10) His appearance to James the Apostle, then to all the apostles (1 Cor 15:7).

28.5.11.en: (11) His appearance to the disciples at the Ascension (Mk 16:19; Lk 24:50, 51; Acts 1:3).

28.5.12.en: In addition to other appearances whose timing the Holy Bible does not specify, but which took place throughout the forty days after His resurrection (Acts 1:3).

28.6.0.en: When the two Marys returned to Jerusalem, some of the soldiers, the guards of the tomb, went to the chief priests and informed them of the resurrection of Christ, the appearance of the angel and the empty tomb. Sadly, the chief priests did not accept faith in the risen Christ. The Gentiles, that is, the soldiers, announce the resurrection to the chief priests of the Jews and do not accept faith, though the opposite should have happened, that is, the Jews should have announced to the Gentiles the resurrection of the awaited Messiah. The chief priests had described Him as a deceiver when they met Pilate to have the tomb sealed, out of fear of His words about His rising three days after His death (ch. 27:62-65). Yet when He rose as He had said, they refused to believe.

28.6.1.en: Accept God's message even if it comes to you on the lips of the people of the world, and repent and return to Him in humility.

28.7.0.en: “The elders”: the members of the council of the Sanhedrin.

28.7.1.en: “Took counsel”: they searched for a reason for the absence of Christ's body from the tomb, in order to mislead the people about His resurrection. The chief priests, with the elders of the Jews, not only refused to believe, but gathered together to oppose the resurrection!! So they gave a bribe of money to the soldiers who guarded the tomb so that they would claim that the disciples of Christ had stolen His body by night, while sleep had overcome them, and the disciples crept in and stole the body.

28.7.2.en: And if the governor Pilate learned of it and became angry with them, the chief priests would appeal to him by virtue of their position, and he would forgive them and not harm them, relying on man's love of money, so that he lies in order to obtain what he wants.

28.8.0.en: The soldiers took the bribe, which was silver, and said what the chief priests had taught them, and the report spread throughout Judea that Christ's body had been stolen. But this is illogical, for how could a group of weak disciples overcome armed soldiers?

28.8.1.en: Or how could the soldiers sleep and not feel the rolling away of a great stone like this one, and the stealing of the body?

28.8.2.en: In addition to the most important thing, which is how can a person know what happens around him while he is asleep?!!

28.8.3.en: The divine providence made the chief priests help to spread the good news of Christ's resurrection without their intending it.

28.8.4.en: “Until this day”: the day Matthew wrote his Gospel, about 30 years after the resurrection of Christ.

28.9.0.en: The disciples hurried joyfully to Galilee to see their Teacher and Beloved on the mountain, where a person is lifted above the world, seeking heavenly things.

28.9.1.en: And when Christ appeared to them, they worshiped Him and rejoiced at meeting Him, even though one of them, Thomas, had doubted when he heard from his brethren the disciples of His appearance to them in the upper room on the day of the resurrection. But Christ appeared to them again while Thomas was with them in the upper room on the Sunday after the resurrection.

28.9.2.en: “But some doubted”: this doubt was an expression of human weakness, as happened with Thomas, but Christ confirmed His resurrection by appearing several times until they believed.

28.10.0.en: “Jesus came”: since He had appeared to them from afar, He afterward drew near to them, and began to teach them after they had been reassured of His resurrection.

28.10.1.en: “All power is given unto Me”: Christ in His life on earth showed His weakness as a man, and suffered and died for us. After His resurrection, He appears to us in the authority of His divinity, and therefore says: “All power is given unto Me,” that is, there appears before you a divine authority over everything in heaven and on earth.

28.10.2.en: “Teach”: preach and teach people faith in Christ.

28.10.3.en: “All nations”: because salvation is for the whole world and not only for the Jews.

28.10.4.en: Christ granted His divine authority to His disciples in the sacrament of the priesthood. He gave them power to teach the whole world the sound faith in His death and resurrection, to care for them in the pastoral care of spiritual discipleship, and to grant them the first of the Holy Sacraments, which is the sacrament of Baptism in the name of the Holy Trinity. This is a clear declaration of the authority of the priesthood that Christ gave to His disciples and their successors to administer the Holy Sacraments to the whole world.

28.11.0.en: After Baptism, they care for them with spiritual teaching in the commandments of Christ so that they may walk by them, He affirming His support for them and for all His priests and ministers of the New Testament until the end of the ages; for He remains with His children to the end.

28.11.1.en: If God is with us, we are not troubled, but go forward in confidence to fulfill His commandments, and even to announce His love to others.

28.11.2.en: There are many proofs of the resurrection of Christ, the most important of which are:

28.11.3.en: (1) His appearing many times, and not once only.

28.11.4.en: (2) His appearing to different people, so it is not the testimony of one person but of a great number. In one of the appearances it was to more than five hundred brethren.

28.11.5.en: (3) His appearing at different times, in the morning, in the evening and at night, so that it can be verified.

28.11.6.en: (4) His appearing over a long period, forty days, which was a sufficient period to verify it.

28.11.7.en: (5) Those to whom He appeared were able to perceive Him with their senses, whether by sight, or by hearing His familiar voice, or by touching Him, and even by eating with them and in their midst.

28.11.8.en: (6) The resurrection of Christ was not expected by His disciples and followers, so it was not a suggestion or imagination, for they were greatly astonished when they learned of His resurrection, and He appeared many times to confirm it.

28.11.9.en: (7) From the strength of His disciples' faith in His resurrection, they preached it throughout the whole world and endured many sufferings, and even sacrificed their lives to complete their proclamation of His resurrection; for a person cannot sacrifice his life for a falsehood that he himself invented.
